title: Klonoa 2: Lunatea's Veil
subtitle: Another dream to enter
summary: Klonoa 2: Lunatea's Veil is Namco's PlayStation 2 platform adventure, first released in Japan on 21 March 2001. Klonoa arrives in the world of Lunatea and travels with the priestess-in-training Lolo and her companion Popka. Their journey crosses kingdoms associated with different emotions as a new danger approaches. The stages follow a largely fixed path through three-dimensional scenery, letting the camera turn around towers and landscapes while movement remains easy to read. Bright colours and expressive characters introduce a story that gradually becomes more melancholy.
body: Klonoa 2: Lunatea's Veil is Namco's PlayStation 2 platform adventure, first released in Japan on 21 March 2001. Klonoa arrives in the world of Lunatea and travels with the priestess-in-training Lolo and her companion Popka. Their journey crosses kingdoms associated with different emotions as a new danger approaches. The stages follow a largely fixed path through three-dimensional scenery, letting the camera turn around towers and landscapes while movement remains easy to read. Bright colours and expressive characters introduce a story that gradually becomes more melancholy.

Klonoa's ring captures enemies that he can carry and throw. Tossing one downward supplies an extra jump, so reaching a ledge depends on bringing the right creature to the right position. Throws can also strike switches or targets in the foreground and background. The player therefore reads enemies as moving tools as well as obstacles. Later stages combine these actions with more demanding timing, asking for a chain of captures and jumps whose solution becomes clear through the arrangement of creatures and platforms.

Board-riding sequences change the pace between the more deliberate platform stages and boss encounters. Collectibles and rescued inhabitants encourage another pass through a familiar Vision, while the world map provides a clear route through the adventure. Critics praised the level design and the use of three-dimensional scenery, although the game sold modestly. Hideo Yoshizawa and Yoshihiko Arawi shaped its story, supported by a large Namco music team. The original PlayStation 2 adventure later returned in the 2022 Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series compilation alongside the first game's remake.
story_headings: An enemy becomes a second jump
A path with room to change
